| [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md) v2 | The Homological Nature of Entropy | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), DOI-10.3390/e17053253. On a finite probability space, take an information structure S (a set of partitions closed under joins that have a common refinement in S and containing the trivial partition) and a probability family Q complete for it. The information cohomology H*(S;Q) is computed by a Hochschild-type bar complex whose action is Shannon's averaged conditioning. If S is connected and "sufficiently rich" and cochains are measurable, then H¹ is one-dimensional and spanned by Shannon entropy (Thm 1). This makes entropy the unique measurable 1-cocycle, up to one multiplicative constant per connected component. In the unitary-invariant quantum case H¹_U = 0: Shannon entropy is the coboundary of minus the von Neumann entropy, which is the unique invariant 0-cochain with that property up to an additive constant (Thm 3). The tree ("arborescent") version again gives H¹ spanned by entropy (Thm 4). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md)); the founding paper of information cohomology, with complete proofs of the degree-one results (Thms 1, 3, 4). Read it for those. Its broader programme (higher mutual informations as cocycles, super/sub-harmonicity, max-entropy discrimination) is sketched or deferred here to unpublished companion papers. |

| [LIT-347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-347.md) v2 | Information-theoretic analysis of generalization capability of learning algorithms | Xu & Raginsky (2017), [ARXIV-1705.07809](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07809). If the loss ℓ(w,Z) is σ-subgaussian for every w, then the expected generalisation error of any learning algorithm P_{W\|S} obeys \|E[L_μ(W) − L_S(W)]\| ≤ √(2σ²·I(S;W)/n) (Theorem 1). This extends Russo–Zou to uncountable hypothesis spaces, and the paper adds a high-probability version, n = (8σ²/α²)(ε/β + log(2/β)) (Theorem 3). Minimising empirical risk plus I(S;W), relaxed to a KL term against a prior Q, yields exactly the Gibbs algorithm (Theorem 5). Noisy ERM and adaptive composition are analysed through the same mutual-information quantity. | Active — read in full 2026-09-29 (NOTE-306); worth reading as the short, clean source of the input–output mutual-information generalisation bound, and of "a learning algorithm is a channel P_{W\|S}", whose capacity is sup_μ I(S;W). The bound is in expectation and is vacuous for deterministic algorithms on continuous hypotheses, which is what the later compression and rate–distortion refinements (LIT-236, LIT-233) address. |

Proves the lower bound on the variance of unbiased estimators in terms of Fisher information (the Cramér–Rao bound), and in the same paper introduces the Fisher-information Riemannian metric and the Rao–Blackwell improvement idea. | Unavailable — seeded 2026-09-29 from metadata and published descriptions, not read: registered because the owner's prior-art novelty map cites it. A close reading was attempted on 2026-09-29 and no legitimate full text could be reached; it stays Unavailable until a copy is supplied. |

| [LIT-356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md) v2 | How much does your data exploration overfit? Controlling bias via information usage | Russo & Zou (2015), arXiv:1511.05219. Suppose an analyst reports statistic φ_T, chosen by any data-dependent rule T from m candidates each σ-sub-Gaussian. Then the selection bias obeys \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) (Prop. 1), where "information usage" I(T;φ) ≤ H(T) ≤ log m. For argmax selection over φ ~ N(µ,I) the squared error is Θ(1 + H(T)) (Prop. 3). Adaptive analyses compose additively, with I(T_{k+1};φ) ≤ Σ_i I(Y_{T_i};φ_{T_i} \| H_{i−1},T_i) (Lemma 1). Answering each query with Gaussian noise of variance σ²√j/n therefore keeps the k-th answer's error at O(σk^{1/4}/√n) (Prop. 7). | Active — read in full 2026-09-29 ([NOTE-308](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-308.md)); Worth reading as the origin of the mutual-information bias and generalisation bound that [LIT-347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-347.md) (Xu & Raginsky) extends, and as the first place its adaptive-composition chain rule and its per-query "information budget" with Gaussian noise (½·log(1+SNR) per query) appear. Read it knowing that it is stated for a finite set of m candidate statistics, and that "the bound is tight" is shown only for Gaussian argmax and threshold selections, as squared-error (not bias) bounds except in the exponential case. |
| [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md) v2 | Notes on Landauer's principle, reversible computation, and Maxwell's Demon | Bennett (2002), arXiv:physics/0210005. Bennett states Landauer's principle as a consequence of the Second Law. A logically irreversible step, meaning erasure or a *merge of control flow*, must export at least the lost entropy (k ln 2 per bit) to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom. That export need not take the form of heat (p. 1). Logically reversible operations, including copying onto a blank register and measurement, have no minimum cost. He calls "an intrinsic cost of order kT for every elementary act of information processing" a 20th-century "misconception" (pp. 5–6). Erasing random data can itself be thermodynamically reversible; the waste comes from applying a many-to-one operation to *known* data (pp. 1, 4). | Active — read in full 2026-09-29 ([NOTE-310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-310.md)); Worth reading as a short, first-hand statement, by the principle's main defender, of what Landauer's principle requires (logical irreversibility) and what it does not (any cost for acquiring, copying or evaluating information). It is the best reachable stand-in for the unreachable [LIT-328](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-328.md). Read it knowing that it is an argued position paper, not a derivation. On the Earman–Norton "unnecessary or insufficient" dilemma Bennett concedes the point "with some justice" (p. 5) and defends the principle only as pedagogy. |
| [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) v2 | The Theory of Signal Detectability. Part I: The General Theory; Part II: Applications with Gaussian Noise | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), <https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/handle/2027.42/7068>. Peterson and Birdsall show that the criterion approach (maximise P_SN(A) − β·P_N(A), or maximise detection at fixed false-alarm k) and the Woodward–Davies a-posteriori approach are all solved by one receiver that computes the likelihood ratio ℓ(x) = f_SN(x)/f_N(x) and thresholds it (Part I, Theorems 1–7). They introduce the receiver operating characteristic, whose slope at each point is the threshold β (Theorem 8, Eq. 2.51). For a signal known exactly in white Gaussian noise, ln ℓ is normal with equal variance 2E/N₀ under both hypotheses and means 2E/N₀ apart, so the ROC is a one-parameter family indexed by the "detection index" d = (M_SN − M_N)²/σ² = 2E/N₀ (Part II, Eqs. 4.1–4.8, Fig. 4.1). The receiver is a correlator or matched filter (Eq. 5.3, 4.10). | Active — read in part 2026-09-30 ([NOTE-315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-315.md)); worth reading as the founding engineering statement of signal detection theory: the likelihood-ratio receiver, the ROC and its slope property, and the equal-variance Gaussian case with an explicit d = 2E/N₀. Read the 1953 report knowing that the scan is poor and that the 1954 IRE paper (with W. C. Fox) is the citable journal form, which was not read here. |
| [LIT-372](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-372.md) v2 | On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning | Saxe et al. (2018), DOI-10.1088/1742-5468/ab3985. Replicating Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby with their own code, the paper shows the information-plane "compression phase" appears only for double-saturating nonlinearities measured through an imposed binning/noise model: tanh compresses, ReLU/softplus/linear do not (binning, KDE, Kraskov; SZT task and MNIST), and re-binning the same tanh run evenly in net input removes it. Compression and generalisation dissociate in all four combinations, full-batch GD compresses as much as SGD, and the drift→diffusion gradient-SNR transition occurs in networks that cannot compress (ReLU, MNIST, a 1-1-1 linear net), so it is real but unrelated to compression. | Active — read in full 2026-09-30 ([NOTE-320](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-320.md)); worth reading as the direct experimental test of all three claims of the IB account of deep learning (two phases; compression causes generalisation; SGD diffusion causes compression), each refuted as a general statement with the original code, and for its Appendix C argument that I(h;X) is infinite in a deterministic network so every finite information-plane value belongs to the analyst's noise model. |
| [LIT-377](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-377.md) | On Context-Content Uncertainty Principle | Li (2025), arXiv:2506.20699 v1. It posits that structured content (priors, schemas) has far lower entropy than context (sensory input), and concludes that inference should run from content to context, minimizing H(context \| content). On that it builds four layers of principles. The first is structure before specificity and its equivalents. The second covers precision-weighted attention, slower learning for content than for context, and memory as low-entropy attractors. The third is staged structure-first learning, and the fourth hierarchical composition. It then reads predictive coding, the free energy principle, active inference and attractor dynamics as instances. Everything is asserted or argued informally. There are no experiments, and several proofs are wrong or missing. | Rejected — by [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md); read in full 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-325](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-325.md)); not worth a reader's time as a source of results. Its foundation is the entropy chain rule plus an assumption, H(content) ≪ H(context), and from these it reads off a direction of inference. Of its eight theorems, one is proved only in sketch, one equivalence proposition is marked "proof skipped" and argued only in words (App. H), and the proofs of Theorems 6–8 swap the roles of content and context relative to the statements. The proof of Theorem 1 states the inequality backwards. Theorem 3 rests on D_KL(q‖p) ≥ H(q) − H(p), which is false in general. The abstract's "computational simulations" are not in the paper. The author's own v2 (June 2026) replaced the whole framework under a new title. |
| [LIT-445](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-445.md) | From the Phenomenology to the Mechanisms of Consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0 | Oizumi, Albantakis & Tononi (2014), PLoS Computational Biology 10(5):e1003588. IIT 3.0 states five axioms of experience (existence, composition, information, integration, exclusion), turns each into a postulate about mechanisms in a state, and identifies an experience with the maximally irreducible conceptual structure of a "complex". Exclusion makes a complex a local maximum of integrated conceptual information Φ over all overlapping sets of elements, so complexes cannot overlap and no subset or superset of a complex is conscious. Worked logic-gate examples show minor complexes beside a major one, an inactive network that is conscious, a minimally conscious photodiode, and a feed-forward "zombie" functionally equivalent to a conscious system. | Active — read in full 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-365.md)), equations excepted; worth reading as the formal statement of the exclusion postulate that Schwitzgebel's 2014 manuscript ([LIT-159](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md)) attacks: "of all overlapping sets of elements, only one set can be conscious", a complex being a local maximum of Φ against every overlapping set. It is IIT's anti-nesting principle, stated as a postulate and motivated only by the phenomenological exclusion axiom; the paper's Occam's-razor argument is given for exclusion within a mechanism, not between systems. It also says plainly that function does not fix consciousness, which is IIT's answer to whether agency built from parts brings experience with it. |
| [LIT-521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md) | Information theory explanation of the fluctuation theorem, maximum entropy production and self-organized criticality in non-equilibrium stationary states | Dewar (2003), DOI-10.1088/0305-4470/36/3/303. It applies Jaynes's maximum-entropy inference to the microscopic paths of an open system in a stationary state. Under fixed initial densities and boundary fluxes plus local conservation, the path distribution is p_Γ ∝ exp(A_Γ), with A_Γ carrying τσ_Γ/2k_B (Eq. 14). A fluctuation theorem and ⟨σ⟩ ≥ 0 follow (Eqs. 18–21). Then, in a mean-field approximation and assuming the number of paths increases with irreversible action, maximizing path entropy over the remaining multipliers is maximizing mean entropy production (MaxEP, Eq. 24). A Landau–Ginzburg argument claims self-organized criticality as slow driving goes to zero. | Active — read in full 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md)); worth reading as the founding attempt to derive the maximum-entropy-production principle (MaxEP) from Jaynes's maximum-entropy inference over microscopic paths, and as the source most later MEP work, Kleidon's included, cites for MEP's theoretical foundation. Read it as a programme, not a proof. The path distribution p_Γ ∝ exp(A_Γ) and its fluctuation theorem follow from the stated constraints. The MaxEP step needs a mean-field approximation and an assumption that the number of paths grows with their irreversible action, which is stated, not argued. The self-organized-criticality corollary is a mean-field artefact by Grinstein and Linsker's analysis ([LIT-525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-525.md)), which this reading confirms. |
| [LIT-522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md) | Entropy production fluctuation theorem and the nonequilibrium work relation for free energy differences | Crooks (1999), DOI-10.1103/PhysRevE.60.2721. For finite classical systems with stochastic, Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production ω of a forward process and of its time reverse satisfy P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^{ω} for any finite time, provided ω is odd under reversal. That holds for processes that start and end in equilibrium, where ω = β(W − ΔF), and for time-symmetric nonequilibrium steady states. The Jarzynski equality follows in one line, and for long times the theorem gives a heat fluctuation theorem and a Gaussian with variance twice the mean. | Active — read in full 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md)); worth reading as the short paper that turned the entropy-production fluctuation theorem into a finite-time, trajectory-level statement for stochastic, microscopically reversible dynamics, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^{ω}, and derived the Jarzynski equality from it in a line. It also defines the trajectory entropy production ω = ln ρ(x_{−τ}) − ln ρ(x_{+τ}) − βQ that the record's stochastic-thermodynamics papers inherit. Read it knowing that its conditions are stated exactly (finite classical system, constant-intensive-parameter baths, Markovian microscopically reversible dynamics, ω odd under time reversal), and that the steady-state version is formally exact but, by the author's own account, of little practical use. |
| [LIT-523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md) | Stochastic thermodynamics, fluctuation theorems and molecular machines | Seifert (2012), DOI-10.1088/0034-4885/75/12/126001. A 105-page review of stochastic thermodynamics. Work, heat and a stochastic system entropy s = −ln p(x(τ),τ) are defined along single trajectories of Markovian systems coupled to baths, and every known integral, detailed and Crooks fluctuation theorem is derived from one master theorem by choosing a conjugate dynamics. Further results: dissipation bounds forward–reverse distinguishability (⟨w⟩ − ΔF ≥ D[p‖p_eq]), Sagawa–Ueda feedback relations, a NESS fluctuation–dissipation theorem in terms of entropy production, and a cycle-based theory of efficiency at maximum power for molecular machines. | Active — read 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md); §§5, 8.3–8.4, 9.2 and 11 skimmed); worth reading as the systematic reference for stochastic thermodynamics as of 2012: first law, heat and stochastic entropy along single trajectories of Markovian systems coupled to baths, every known fluctuation theorem derived from one master theorem with a conjugate dynamics, dissipation as distinguishability of forward and reverse paths, Sagawa–Ueda feedback, the NESS fluctuation–dissipation theorem and efficiency of molecular machines. It is the framework in which the record's thermodynamics-of-prediction and thermodynamics-of-learning results ([LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md), [LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) are stated. Read it as a review: the derivations are its own and concise, the case studies are reported. |
| [LIT-525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-525.md) | Comments on a derivation and application of the ‘maximum entropy production’ principle | Grinstein & Linsker (2007), DOI-10.1088/1751-8113/40/31/N01. A Comment with two points. (1) Dewar's 2005 derivation of MaxEP needs a quadratic approximation to p(f) near f = F to hold for all f. With the fluctuation theorem, that forces A(F) to be constant, i.e. linear constitutive relations. So the "orthogonality condition" behind both maximum and minimum entropy production fails far from equilibrium, as an exact spin-chain model shows. (2) Dewar's 2003 SOC result is an artefact. Keeping the quartic term gives a finite flux variance at F_ext = 0. | Active — read in full 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-422.md)); worth reading as the short, exact critique of Dewar's information-theoretic derivation of maximum entropy production. It shows that the 2005 derivation's key step holds only where the constitutive relations are linear, so MaxEP far from equilibrium is not established by it, and that the 2003 claim that MaxEP yields self-organized criticality is an artefact of a mean-field expansion. Read from the authors' submitted manuscript (Zenodo); the version of record was not seen. Its first point is checked here only on its own worked example, since Dewar 2005 itself could not be read. |
| [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md) | Sophisticated Inference | Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp & Parr (2021; arXiv 2020), Neural Computation 33(3):713–763. Ordinary active inference scores a fixed set of policies by expected free energy (risk plus ambiguity). Sophisticated inference instead evaluates the expected free energy of the next action recursively, averaging over the beliefs the agent would hold after each plausible outcome and action, which amounts to a tree search over belief states pruned below a probability of 1/16. In simulations it plans past short-term costs: a rat visits a mildly aversive cue, and a horizon of four escapes a local minimum in a maze. It recovers Bayes-adaptive RL in the zero-temperature limit. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md)), from the arXiv preprint, whose displayed equations did not survive text extraction. Worth reading as the active-inference planning scheme the record's free-energy holdings otherwise lack: expected free energy evaluated recursively over future belief states, a deep tree search pruned by probability, with the Bellman equation as its formal analogue. The evidence is small simulations (a T-maze rat and an 8 × 8 grid). Flagged anthology-candidate: it is a planning algorithm, compared with reinforcement learning, and the anthology's agents-and-environments topic may hold it. |
| [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md) | Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), PNAS 117(40). Training past zero error (the terminal phase, TPT) drives four linked phenomena in the last layer: within-class variability collapses (Tr(Σ_WΣ_B†)/C → 0), centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosines −1/(C−1), a simplex ETF; classifier rows become proportional to the means; and the decision becomes nearest class mean. Measured on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10/100, STL10 and ImageNet with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet, 480 models. Test accuracy and DeepFool robustness keep improving during TPT. Theorems: NC1–NC2 imply NC3–NC4 for the Webb–Lowe and Soudry max-margin classifiers, and the simplex ETF uniquely maximizes the small-noise error exponent. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-476](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-476.md)); worth reading as the source of neural collapse: in the terminal phase of training, last-layer features collapse to their class means (NC1), the centred means form a simplex equiangular tight frame (NC2), the classifier aligns with them (NC3) and the decision becomes nearest class centre (NC4). Measured on 7 datasets × 3 architectures; NC1–NC2 imply NC3–NC4 for the Webb–Lowe and max-margin classifiers, and the simplex ETF is the unique optimal codebook in a vanishing-noise Gaussian channel. It explains Papyan's Hessian outliers as class means outgrowing collapsing within-class variation. |
| [LIT-764](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-764.md) | A Mathematical Theory of Communication | Shannon (1948), Bell System Technical Journal 27:379–423 and 623–656. The founding paper of information theory: entropy as the measure of information, the source coding theorem, channel capacity, and the theorem that a noisy channel can carry information at any rate below capacity with arbitrarily small error. Also: the noiseless capacity of constrained channels, equivocation as the information a receiver lacks, C = W log(1 + P/N) for white noise, and the minimum rate for a continuous source at a stated fidelity. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md)); worth reading as the source of the measure and both coding theorems, in their first and plainest form: a source's entropy is the minimum rate it can be sent at (Theorem 9), a noisy channel's capacity C = max(H(x) − H_y(x)) is the maximum rate at which error can be made arbitrarily small, and errors do not force the rate to zero (Theorem 11, by averaging over random codes). Shannon says the axioms that single out −Σ p log p are not needed by the theory; the coding theorems are its justification. The capacity formula W log(1 + P/N) and the sampling representation are already here (Theorems 13, 17), as is the minimum rate for a source at a given fidelity (Theorem 21). Proofs are sketches at the typical-set level. |

Filed, not read; only the publisher's table of contents and preview chapter were read. | Unavailable — filed 2026-10-09 from Crossref, not read: no lawful full text exists to reach. The rate- distortion function when the decoder, but not the encoder, sees correlated side information: a single-letter characterisation, with a rate loss relative to the case where both see it, zero in the Gaussian case. Filed, not read: no lawful full text was reached. | Unavailable — filed 2026-10-09 from Crossref, not read: no lawful full text was reached. | [LIT-778](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-778.md) v2 | Comparison of Statistical Experiments | Torgersen (1991), Cambridge University Press. The comprehensive treatment of comparing statistical experiments, from Wald, Blackwell and Le Cam: when one experiment is more informative than another, Le Cam's deficiency as the measure of the difference, and its relations to sufficiency and randomisation. Not read: no lawful full text. | Unavailable — filed 2026-10-09 from Crossref and the publisher's pages, not read: no lawful full text was reachable. | [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md) | Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments | Blackwell (1953), Ann. Math. Statist. 24(2):265–272. Completes the Blackwell order: for finitely many states, one experiment is at least as informative as another for every decision problem exactly when the other is a garbling of it. The easy direction is Blackwell (1951) and the finite converse Sherman and Stein's; this paper re-proves the converse by minimax, extends it to arbitrary outcome spaces by a martingale argument, introduces comparison by k-action problems, and reduces two-state comparison to the type I/type II error trade-off. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md)); worth reading as the paper in which the comparison of experiments is settled in general: for experiments with finitely many states, being at least as informative in every decision problem (Bohnenblust, Shapley and Sherman's order) and being able to reproduce the other by a stochastic transformation (Blackwell's 1951 sufficiency, later called garbling) are the same order. The finite-outcome converse is Sherman and Stein's, re-proved here by a minimax argument; the extension to arbitrary outcome spaces, by martingale convergence, is new. It adds comparison by k-action problems, and shows that for two states testing problems, and so the type I/type II error curves, decide the order. |
| [LIT-793](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-793.md) | Semantic Rate-Distortion Theory with Applications | Zhao, Ma, Li, Yuan, Ye & Zhou (2025), arXiv. Defines semantic distortion as a divergence between the posteriors of a latent meaning S given the original and the reconstructed observation, proves that the information rate–distortion function under this and a symbolic constraint is the operational limit (given lower semicontinuity), and solves the doubly symmetric binary case with total variation and Hamming distortion. With KL divergence the function is the information bottleneck, which the paper does not note. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-638](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-638.md)); worth reading as the formal version of "preserve the distribution over interpretations, not one meaning": the semantic distortion compares the posterior of the meaning S given the original observation with its posterior given the reconstruction, alongside an ordinary distortion on the symbols, and the paper proves the coding theorem for the resulting rate–distortion function and solves a binary case. Read it knowing three things the paper does not say. With Kullback–Leibler divergence its expected semantic distortion is exactly I(S;X) − I(S;Y), so its function is the information bottleneck; with total variation it bounds the extra Bayes risk of every bounded-loss decision about S. Its sequence distortion is defined as a maximum inside the expectation, while both proofs use the maximum of per-letter expectations, so the theorems hold for the latter. And its MNIST experiment trains with a classifier's cross-entropy against the true label, not with the posterior distortion the theory defines. |
| [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md) | Efficient compression in color naming and its evolution | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), PNAS 115(31):7937–7942. Treats a language's colour lexicon as an information-bottleneck encoder from perceptual meanings to words and finds the World Color Survey's 110 languages, and English, near the IB complexity–accuracy bound, with one trade-off parameter β (fitted values just above 1) accounting for much of the variation between them. IB optima have soft boundaries and inconsistently named regions, as the data do, and the IB path through β passes through structural phase transitions that roughly recapitulate Berlin and Kay's sequence, apart from an early yellow category the data lack. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md)); worth reading as the paper that puts the information bottleneck to work on word meanings: a lexicon is an encoder q(w\|m) from meanings (Gaussians over CIELAB colour) to words, scored by complexity I(M;W) against accuracy I(W;U), and the colour-naming systems of the World Color Survey and English lie close to the IB curve at β only slightly above 1, with 93% beating all 39 hue-rotated variants of themselves. Read it knowing that the need distribution (the LI source) is estimated from the naming data, cross-validated over languages, and that the "evolution" is a reading of the annealing path along the curve, not a model of historical change. Source of [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). |
| [LIT-812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-812.md) | Rate-Distortion-Perception Theory for Semantic Communication | Chai, Xiao, Shi & Saad (2023), IEEE ICNP 2023 workshop. Models a semantic source S seen by the encoder only through X, with Wyner–Ziv side information and common randomness, and states the rate needed to reproduce S within an expected distortion and a total-variation bound on its distribution. Closed form for a doubly symmetric binary source: recovering X exactly does not recover S, and with side information the rate reaches zero at a non-trivial distortion. Proofs sketched. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-605](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-605.md)); worth reading as a short statement of semantic communication as indirect (remote) source coding with a perception constraint: the encoder sees only a noisy observation X of the semantic source S, the decoder must reproduce S within an expected distortion and within a total-variation distance of S's distribution, and side information Y may help. It gives a rate region, a closed form for a doubly symmetric binary source, and an MNIST illustration. Read it knowing that it is a six-page workshop paper whose proofs are sketched or omitted, that the region as printed mixes channel and source terms and does not define the reconstruction, and that its "zero-rate recovery" is the familiar fact that a decoder with side information needs no bits once the tolerated distortion is what the side information alone achieves. |
| [LIT-823](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-823.md) | Semantic Communication: A Survey of Its Theoretical Development | Xin, Fan & Letaief (2024), Entropy 26(2):102. A survey of semantic information theory: semantic entropy (logical probability, task-, knowledge- and context-based variants), semantic rate–distortion with meaning as a latent state behind the observation, semantic noise and semantic channel capacity, and the information bottleneck, age of information, joint source–channel coding and LLMs as tools. It records that no unified framework exists. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-619](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-619.md)); worth reading as a map of what "semantic information theory" has meant from Carnap and Bar-Hillel to deep-learning semantic communication: logical-probability and knowledge-base definitions of semantic entropy, a semantic rate–distortion function in which meaning is a hidden state S observed through X, semantic channel capacities that can exceed Shannon capacity by tolerating bit errors, and the information bottleneck, age of information, joint source–channel coding and LLMs as tools. It is a catalogue, not a synthesis: it states that no agreed framework exists, compares the definitions only informally, and does not cover rate–distortion–perception work. One formula is misstated (the bottleneck constraint is written with its inequality reversed). |
| [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md) | Informative Communication in Word Production and Word Learning | Frank, Goodman, Lai & Tenenbaum (2009), Proceedings of CogSci 31, pp. 1228–1233. A speaker who chooses words to minimise the KL divergence between her intended meaning and a word's literal meaning picks, for a known referent, a true word with probability ∝ \|w\|^(−α): the size principle, derived from communication. Word learners' bets about a novel word's meaning fit the inverted model at r = .93; speakers' free descriptions follow it only weakly (r = .19, and not at all for colour terms). | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md)); worth reading as the paper that first writes the informative speaker down: a speaker soft-maximises the utility −D_KL(M_S ‖ w̃), the information lost about her intended meaning when it is replaced by the uniform distribution over a word's extension, so for a known referent she picks a true word with probability ∝ \|w\|^(−α), the size principle derived from communicative premises. A learner who knows the referent inverts that speaker to infer what a novel word means; 700 web participants' bets track the model's predictions (r = .93). In a free-description task speakers' use of Flickr tag-words correlates only weakly with informativeness (r = .19 overall, .51 without colour terms, .02 for colour terms). It has no listener inferring a referent and no recursion: that step is Frank and Goodman 2012 ([LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md)). |
| [LIT-868](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-868.md) | A Generalized Information-Theoretic Framework for the Emergence of Hierarchical Abstractions in Resource-Limited Systems | Larsson, Maity and Tsiotras (2022), Entropy 24(6):809. Treats a pruning of a fixed quadtree as a deterministic encoder of the grid and maximises Σβ_i I(T;Y_i) − Σγ_j I(T;Z_j) − αI(T;X) over such prunings. Every term splits over interior nodes (p(t)·JS of the children's conditionals; p(t)H of the split), so a bottom-up recursion (G-tree search) returns the optimal tree with fewest leaves in linear time. Recovers the IB and IB-with-side-information trees as special cases and proves the latter is always a pruning of the former. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md)); worth reading as an exact solution of a structured information-bottleneck problem: when the encoder must be a pruning of a fixed tree (here the dyadic quadtree of a grid), every information term splits over the interior nodes, a node's share of I(T;Y) being p(t) times the Jensen–Shannon divergence of its children's p(y\|·) and its share of I(T;X) being p(t)H(Π). A bottom-up recursion, G(t) = max{ΔJ(t) + Σ G(children), 0}, then returns the optimal tree with the fewest leaves for any weighted sum of relevance, irrelevance and compression terms, in time linear in the grid. A greedy top-down search can miss all the relevant information, because a node whose children predict Y alike gains nothing however much its grandchildren differ. Adding an irrelevance penalty can only prune the plain IB tree. The hierarchy is given, not found: what "emerges" is which coarse-graining of a fixed quadtree to keep. |
| [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md) v2 | Mutual information, neural networks and the renormalization group | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017; Nature Physics 14, 578–582, 2018). Defines the relevant degrees of freedom of a spatial block as the coarse variable that maximizes mutual information with the environment beyond a buffer, and learns it with restricted Boltzmann machines from Monte Carlo samples (the RSMI algorithm). It recovers Kadanoff block spins in the 2D Ising model and the electric-field variables of the dimer model, ignores decoupled noise, and, iterated, gives the Ising flow and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15; a distribution-fitting RBM does none of this. The link to a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is proved only in 1D. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-674](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-674.md)); worth reading as the paper that turns "the relevant degrees of freedom" of real-space renormalization into an objective that can be optimized: a block's coarse variable is chosen to maximize its mutual information with the system beyond a buffer around the block. Trained on Monte Carlo samples alone, the network rediscovers Kadanoff's block spin for the 2D Ising model, finds the low-momentum electric fields of the 2D dimer model while ignoring a strongly patterned but decoupled noise, and, iterated, reproduces the Ising flow away from T_c (located to about 1%) with ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15. An RBM trained instead to fit the data distribution latches on to the noise. The equivalence of the objective with a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is argued, and shown only for 1D and quasi-1D chains; in 2D the evidence is the two models, whose answers were known beforehand. |
| [LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md) | Hippocampal spatial representations exhibit a hyperbolic geometry that expands with experience | Zhang, Rich, Lee & Sharpee (2022 online, Nat. Neurosci. 26, 2023). The pairwise correlations of rat dorsal CA1 place cells have the topological signature of points sampled uniformly from a three-dimensional hyperbolic ball, not of a low-dimensional Euclidean cube, and the ball's radius grows with the logarithm of exploration time. Place-field sizes are near exponential, and in a Poisson model exponential sizes carry more positional Fisher information than uniform or log-normal ones, with an optimal radius that matches the measured one for the number of CA1 neurons. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-668](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-668.md)); worth reading as, on its own account, the first evidence that neural responses, not stimuli, carry a hyperbolic geometry. Pairwise spike-train correlations of a few dozen active dorsal CA1 cells per session (34 to 56 in the sessions shown), in rats on a novel 48-m track, a 2.5-m track and a 1.8-m box, give Betti curves (clique topology, invariant to any monotone transform of the correlations) that match points sampled uniformly from a 3D hyperbolic ball and fail to match uniform samples from Euclidean cubes of low dimension or shuffled spikes. The fitted radius (10.5–15.5 in units of inverse curvature) grows with the logarithm of exploration time, on scales from seconds to days, as the maximal information acquirable does. Place-field sizes are close to exponential, as the model requires, and in simulation exponentially distributed field sizes give more Fisher information than uniform or log-normal ones, with an optimal radius growing as log N that extrapolates to the radius measured. The "hierarchy" is one of nested place-field sizes; no tree is recovered from the data, and the only null geometry tested is Euclidean with uniform sampling. |

Lett. 127, 240603). Replaces the RBM estimator of [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md) with a neural InfoNCE lower bound co-trained with a convolutional coarse-graining filter (RSMI-NE), and uses the optimal filters at a single buffer size, not an iterated flow, as lattice forms of the most relevant operators. On the interacting dimer model they are the columnar and plaquette order parameters below T_BKT and the electric fields at high T; the maximal information marks the phases; one fitted scaling dimension (1.00037 against 1) is given. The optimality theorem is cited, not proved here. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-681](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-681.md)); worth reading as the paper that turns the real-space mutual-information principle of [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md) from an iterated coarse-graining into a single-shot extraction of operators: with the mutual information estimated by a neural InfoNCE bound and the coarse-graining a convolutional filter trained against it, the filters that best compress what a block shares with its distant environment are, across the whole phase diagram of the interacting dimer model, the columnar and plaquette order parameters below the BKT transition and the electric fields at high temperature, and the plaquette filter's correlator gives a scaling dimension of 1.00037 against the predicted 1. The maximal information itself, log 4 in the ordered phase and decaying algebraically with the buffer in the critical one, traces the phase diagram. The theorem that the optimal filters are the most relevant operators is cited to another paper, and the model's operators were known beforehand. |
| [LIT-881](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-881.md) v2 | Optimal Renormalization Group Transformation from Information Theory | Lenggenhager, Gökmen, Ringel, Huber and Koch-Janusz (2018; Phys. Rev. X 10, 011037, 2020). Proves that a block coarse-graining keeping all the mutual information the block shares with the system beyond a buffer makes the coarse measure factorize across the block, so a finite-range Hamiltonian gains no range (1D; D dimensions under an extra assumption) and 1D disorder gains no correlations across it. For blocks of two spins of the 1D clean and dilute random Ising chain, where that condition is not met, couplings beyond nearest neighbour and disorder correlations shrink as more information is kept, vanishing at decimation. Encoding into a single binary spin explains why decimation wins in 1D and majority rule in a 2D toy model. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-682](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-682.md)); worth reading as the theory written for the RSMI algorithm of LIT-873: it proves that a coarse-graining which keeps all the information a block shares with the system beyond a buffer factorizes the coarse measure across that block, so a finite-range Hamiltonian does not gain range (in 1D; in D dimensions under an extra per-block assumption) and, for 1D disorder, no correlations are generated across the block. The full-capture condition is not met by the coarse-grainings it then studies: in its own 1D Ising example decimation keeps about half of the block's information, and the decay of next-nearest-neighbour and four-spin couplings, and of disorder correlations, as information grows is shown numerically for blocks of two spins. Its other result is information-theoretic: a single binary block spin loses information by encoding, which is why decimation beats majority rule in 1D and majority rule wins in a 2D toy model. |
| [LIT-885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-885.md) | Relevance in the Renormalization Group and in Information Theory | Gordon, Banerjee, Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2020; Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 240601, 2021). On a cylinder, with block and environment as slabs separated by a buffer of length L_B, the information-bottleneck encoder just past its first transition depends on the block only through the boundary weak value of the leading transfer-matrix eigenvector, the lowest-dimension primary at large circumference, and the transition is at β_c = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B). Checked on a three-site critical Ising cylinder. With a large enough alphabet the encoder respects the data's symmetry near that transition; a small one can break it. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-690](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-690.md)); worth reading as the theorem the real-space mutual-information programme ([LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), [LIT-881](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-881.md), [LIT-878](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-878.md)) cites for its claim that the optimal coarse-graining picks out the most relevant operators. What it proves is narrower than that claim: for a short-range lattice model on a cylinder, with the block and the environment taken as whole slabs of the cylinder separated by a buffer, the information-bottleneck encoder just past its first transition depends on the block only through the boundary weak value of the leading transfer-matrix eigenvector, and the transition sits at β_c = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B); for large circumference that eigenvector is the lowest-dimension primary. The planar block-in-a-shell geometry the algorithms use, the fixed-alphabet β → ∞ limit that is RSMI, and the regime beyond the first transition are not covered. A second result: past the first transition, with a large enough alphabet and no fine-tuning, the optimal encoder carries a representation of the data's symmetry, and a two-symbol example with Z4 symmetry breaks it. |
| [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md) | Deriving Neural Scaling Laws from the statistics of natural language | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), ICML 2026. The data-limited scaling exponent of a language model's test loss is predicted from two measured statistics of the corpus: β, the decay of token–token covariance with lag, which sets the usable context n*(P) ~ P^(1/(2β)), and γ, the decay of next-token conditional entropy with context length. When learning within that context is fast, the loss falls as P^(−γ/(2β)); on TinyStories and WikiText-103 transformers match the predicted 0.185 and 0.141 up to about 10^8 tokens. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md)); worth reading as the sequel to [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md) that takes its effective-context argument from character-level toy runs to subword-tokenised text and a predicted exponent. Two statistics of a corpus are measured: β, the decay with lag n of the largest singular value of the token–token covariance matrix (‖C(n)‖_op ~ n^(−β)), and γ, the decay of the next-token conditional entropy with context length (H_n − H_∞ ~ n^(−γ), a differential form of Hilberg's hypothesis). A signal-to-noise argument gives the horizon n*(P) ~ P^(1/(2β)) a sample of P tokens can use; if learning within that horizon is fast, the test loss falls as P^(−γ/(2β)), and in general as P^(−min(δ, γ/(2β))), with δ the decay of the within-horizon excess loss (App. A, an ansatz-based derivation, not a theorem). Measured on TinyStories (β ≈ 0.88, γ ≈ 0.325, predicted α ≈ 0.185) and WikiText-103 (β ≈ 0.94, γ ≈ 0.265, α ≈ 0.141) with GPT-2- and LLaMA-style transformers up to about 10^8 tokens; the empirical exponents fall inside the predicted intervals and the n-gram losses collapse under P/n^(2β), L_n n^γ. γ is read off the n-gram losses of the largest trained models, not computed from the text alone. Usable horizons reached are a few tens of tokens. No embedding, PMI or hierarchy is studied. |

At the optimum the receiver is certain when she takes the sender's worst action and indifferent otherwise. | [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md) | Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro | Hoel, Albantakis and Tononi (2013), PNAS 110(49). Effective information, the mutual information between uniformly imposed interventions and their effects, equals effectiveness (determinism minus degeneracy) times the log of the state-space size. Coarse-graining always loses size and can gain effectiveness, so in four toy systems of logic gates a macro description carries 0.40 to 2.92 bits more than the micro it supervenes on. The claim that the EI peak is where causation happens rests on the uniform intervention distribution imposed at each level. | Active — read in full 2026-10-13 ([NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md)) from the PubMed Central PDF of the published article (PMC3856819, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3856819/pdf/pnas.201314922.pdf), fetched through the Internet Archive capture of 2022-11-13 because PMC answered scripted requests with a reCAPTCHA page and pnas.org returned 403; the online Supporting Information was not read. Worth reading as the source of effective information as a measure of causal emergence: it shows exactly when a coarse-grained description of a known mechanism can carry more EI than the micro, and its macro advantage rests on imposing a uniform intervention distribution at each level. For [QUESTION-093](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md) it is an interventional criterion met with no closure and no self-individuation; it complements [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) and [THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) and is neither a case nor a rival of them; it measures a different object from the information-decomposition account of [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md). |
| [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md) | A Pseudorandom Generator from any One-way Function | Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), SIAM Journal on Computing 28(4). There is a pseudorandom generator if and only if there is a one-way function (Theorem 6.2.2), in the uniform setting: adversaries are algorithms, and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine that turns an adversary for the constructed generator into an inverter for the given function. The route runs one-way function → false entropy generator → pseudoentropy generator → pseudorandom generator, where "computational entropy" is the Shannon entropy of some P-samplable distribution that no adversary of the given strength tells apart from the output. The general reduction is only weak-preserving: composed literally it needs seeds of length n^34, and the paper's direct construction n^10. The paper attributes to Goldreich [G : 89] the equivalence of pseudorandom generators with P-samplable pairs that are computationally indistinguishable but statistically very different; with Theorem 6.2.2 that gives the one-way function form, but the paper never writes that combined sentence. | Active — read in full 2026-10-15 from the authors' copy on Johan Håstad's KTH page (www.csc.kth.se/~johanh/prgfromowf.pdf, a 46-page typescript, linked from ~johanh/papers.html; not the typeset SIAM pages 1364–1396, which were not checked). Unpaywall and OpenAlex report the DOI closed; OpenAlex lists two CiteSeerX records (10.1.1.35.3930, 10.1.1.36.6283), not needed once the KTH copy was found. Worth reading as the source of the uniform theorem "There are one-way functions iff there are pseudorandom generators" (Theorem 6.2.2) and of computational entropy: the Shannon entropy of a P-samplable distribution that no adversary of a given time-success ratio tells apart from the output, with pseudoentropy (more than the input's entropy) and false entropy (more than the output's own) as the intermediate primitives. All adversaries are uniform and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine; there are no circuits and no min-entropy in the paper, and the general reduction is only weak-preserving (seed length n^10 even in the direct construction). For [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) and [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) it shows that "if pseudorandom generators exist" may be read "if one-way functions exist", and that the claims' rendering G(U_n) is a false entropy generator with false entropy at least n, which names the gap they construct. For [LIT-1053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1053.md) it states, in Section 8, that Goldreich's note [cited as ICSI TR-89-051, July 1989] shows pseudorandom generators equivalent to "a pair of P-samplable distributions which are computationally indistinguishable but statistically very different"; the one-way-function form follows only by combining that with Theorem 6.2.2, which the paper does not write out. For [QUESTION-110](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-110.md) its time-success ratio is a worked cost-of-recovery measure that folds the success criterion into the cost, and for [QUESTION-103](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-103.md) its distinguishing advantage is hit rate minus false-alarm rate, described by the paper itself as "the computationally restricted adversary definition of statistical distance"; it says nothing about real observers. |
| [LIT-1053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1053.md) | A note on computational indistinguishability | Goldreich (1990), Information Processing Letters 34(6), 277–281. As cited in Goldreich's Foundations of Cryptography (§3.8.2 of the 1995 draft): a pair of polynomial-time constructible ensembles that are computationally indistinguishable yet statistically far apart exists if and only if one-way functions exist. Not yet read; the summary is the book's description. | Unavailable — filed 2026-10-15, not read. A lawful full text exists but could not be fetched from this environment on 2026-10-15: found but could not be fetched. Goldreich posts the paper on his Weizmann pages as www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/PSX/iplnote.pdf, linked from his list of papers (~oded/papers.html, where it is dated 1989) and from his annotated bibliography (~oded/annot/node47.html). Web search indexes that PDF; the search tool's summary of it, which was not checked against the text, says it began as a Technion technical report of January 1990 and that it states the existence of pseudorandom generators to be equivalent to the existence of efficiently constructible distributions that are computationally indistinguishable yet statistically far apart. That differs from the book's paraphrase, which says one-way functions. It cannot be settled without the text. Places looked, and what each gave: Unpaywall reports the DOI closed, with no OA location and no repository copy; OpenAlex reports it closed, with no repository full text, listing only the DOI and two CiteSeerX records (10.1.1.145.7487, 10.1.1.39.458); Semantic Scholar gives openAccessPdf status CLOSED; the Elsevier article API reports openaccess 0 and openArchiveArticle false, and ScienceDirect returned 403, so IPL 34(6) is not in Elsevier's open archive; Crossref lists only text-mining links under Elsevier's TDM licence; DBLP served a bot challenge. Goldreich's PDF itself was requested 22 times over about 20 minutes: https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il gave an empty reply every time, http://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il gave 503 every time ("upstream connect error … connection termination"), and https://wisdom.weizmann.ac.il was refused by the proxy (502). WebFetch also got 503 for the PDF. The Internet Archive's availability API reports a capture of the PDF dated 2026-01-23 (web.archive.org/web/20260123154034/https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/PSX/iplnote.pdf). web.archive.org and wayback.archive.org reset every connection from here, about 25 attempts in all; plain http to web.archive.org gave 403; WebFetch refuses web.archive.org; archive.ph also reset. The availability API has no capture of papers.html or of a .ps version. CiteSeerX's download links now redirect to the Internet Archive, so they failed in the same way. The ECCC hosts (eccc.weizmann.ac.il, eccc.uni-trier.de) do not mirror Goldreich's ~oded pages; they return their generic HTML page. The paper can probably be read once the Weizmann server or web.archive.org can be reached from this environment, or from any ordinary browser. What it says is known here only through Goldreich's Foundations of Cryptography ([LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), §3.8.2), which cites it for the equivalence with one-way functions without proving it. |
| [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md) | Foundations of Cryptography | Goldreich (2001), Cambridge University Press. Volume 1 of the standard treatment of the complexity-theoretic foundations of cryptography: one-way functions, computational indistinguishability, pseudorandom generators and zero-knowledge proofs. | Active — read in part 2026-10-15 (Skimmed), and not in its printed form. The text read is the author's 1995 draft, "Foundations of Cryptography (Fragments of a Book)" (23 February 1995, with the "Additional Fragment (Nr. 1)" of 9 February 1996), which Goldreich posted through ECCC (eccc.weizmann.ac.il/static/books/Foundations_of_Cryptography_Fragments_of_a_Book/; PDF at eccc.weizmann.ac.il/resources/pdf/foc.pdf, 305 pp.). The draft's Chapters 1–3 were read in full; its zero-knowledge chapter, the 1989 annotated references and the 1996 addendum were not. The 2001 Cambridge text (DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511546891) is closed: Unpaywall and OpenAlex list no open location. The author's own pages (wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/foc-book.html and related) and the Internet Archive's capture of foc-book.html could not be reached from this environment. Worth reading as the standard source of the definitions of computational indistinguishability (Def. 3.2) and of a pseudorandom generator (Def. 3.9), and for the result that the first is strictly coarser than statistical closeness. For [CASE-083](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-083.md) it confirms each ingredient: the generator definition, the 2⁻ⁿ image count (§3.3.1, stated there only as Δ ≥ ½ with Δ the unhalved sum; the count reappears in the proof of Prop. 3.13), and closure under efficient post-processing, which is set as Exercise 1 of §3.8.4 rather than proved. For [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) it shows that the separation itself needs no assumption: Prop. 3.3 gives, by counting, an ensemble on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no polynomial-time test tells from uniform. Generators, or equivalently one-way functions, are needed only for an efficiently samplable pair (Goldreich 1990, cited in §3.8.2). Indistinguishability is defined only for ensembles indexed by n, never for a single pair of distributions. For [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) it supplies the definitions; the encoding is the record's own. Section numbers are the draft's; the printed volume (Ch. 3 at pp. 101–183) was not checked. |

| [LIT-1151](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1151.md) v2 | Optimal compression of approximate inner products and dimension reduction | Alon & Klartag (2017), FOCS 2017, [ARXIV-1610.00239](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.00239). For n points of norm at most 1 in R^k and 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, storing every inner product and squared distance to additive ε takes Θ(n log n/ε²) bits once k ≥ log n/ε², Θ(nk log(2 + log n/(ε²k))) for log n ≤ k ≤ log n/ε², and Θ(nk log(1/ε)) below, with an efficient per-point sketch. For a target X and sources Y, Z, defines the unique information of Y as the minimum of MI_Q(X:Y\|Z) over Δ_P, the joint distributions with the same (X,Y) and (X,Z) marginals as P; shared and synergistic information follow from the consistency equations. If unique information depends only on the pair marginals, these functions bound every other such measure (Lemma 3). The unique information is zero exactly when Z is Blackwell-sufficient for Y with respect to X (Lemma 6, Corollary 7). The three measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate PI axioms and the identity property, and are computed by a convex programme. Read it knowing that it is bivariate only (it cannot be extended to the PI lattice for three sources, by its own §6), that its optimisation is ill-conditioned in practice (Example 31), and that Table 1's Unq and Copy rows conflict with its own Proposition 18. With Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}, both transfer entropies are 0 and the causation entropies are 1 bit each. By PID, transfer entropy is unique plus synergistic information; only the unique part is a candidate for flow. Network control energy rises under anaesthesia and correlates negatively with ΦR. Regional ΦR loss is largest in unimodal cortex and follows cortical PVALB expression in human, macaque and mouse. Species-specific mean-field models reproduce the PVALB effect and the advantage of central over ventrolateral thalamic stimulation. The target is behavioural responsiveness. | Active — read in full 2026-10-22 ([NOTE-1064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1064.md)) from the publisher's open-access version of record (CC BY 4.0); worth reading as the cross-species, causal extension of the same group's synergistic-workspace result ([LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md)): pairwise integrated information ΦR from resting fMRI falls under anaesthesia in humans, macaques, marmosets and mice and returns with responsiveness, including when central thalamic stimulation re-awakens two anaesthetized macaques, and it tracks arousal better than the original Φ, causal density or functional connectivity. Its main limit is the target: behavioural responsiveness, which the authors call "presumably consciousness" and an "imperfect marker". It is also pairwise, linear-Gaussian, at rest and content-free, and the causal arm rests on two animals. The PVALB and modelling results are correlational and model-bound. Filed as [THEORY-881](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-881.md). |
| [LIT-1376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1376.md) v2 | The Ledger of Will: Evidence, Revaluation, and the Preservation of Revisable Agency | Aevyra (2026). A formal account of memory for persistent agents whose central requirement is "revision sufficiency": retained state must support a declared family of future questions, interventions and changes of evaluative law. It characterizes exact revision sufficiency for finite histories by a factorization condition, derives a lower bound on representation size, and proposes an architecture that keeps grounds and counterevidence with each commitment. | Active — read in full 2026-10-22 ([NOTE-1091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1091.md)) from the web page, version 4.0 of 25 September 2026, with its PDF and reproducibility archive, whose checks were run and reproduce; worth reading as a careful, self-limiting formal statement of what a reduced memory must keep for an agent to stay able to revise: exact sufficiency for a declared family of future demands is factorization through the retained state (the record's [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md)), and under repeated declared revisions it is the coarsest revision-invariant refinement (Moore–Nerode), filed as [THEORY-884](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-884.md). Elementary and, by its authors' account, a synthesis; its architecture and experiment are proposals, unexecuted. It is the closest outside statement of [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) and answers [QUESTION-112](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-112.md) only for a revision family declared in advance. Despite its title it has nothing on will-organization in the record's sense. |
